record.title: Planar omega-decomposition conjecture for graphs of treewidth three
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph of treewidth $3$. A **planar $\omega$-decomposition** is the decomposition notion used in the source, with width, order, and vertex spread as its associated parameters; for a vertex $v$, let $\deg(v)$ denote its degree.

**Planar $\omega$-decomposition conjecture.** Every graph $G$ with treewidth $3$ has a planar $\omega$-decomposition of width $??$ and order $??\cdot |G|$, in which the spread of each vertex $v$ is at most $??\cdot\deg(v)$.

This is posed as a question after the paper discusses a width–spread tradeoff for tree decompositions of graphs of treewidth at most $2$. The constants are unspecified in the source, and no resolution is supplied.
record.source_name: Vida Dujmović, Ken-ichi Kawarabayashi, Bojan Mohar and David R. Wood, “Tight Upper Bounds on the Crossing Number in a Minor-Closed Class”, arXiv:1807.11617 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.11617

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2018).

record.title: Polynomial-time recognition conjecture for good orderings of 2T-graphs
record.statement: A **2T-graph** is a graph consisting of two edge-disjoint spanning trees. A **good ordering** is an ordering of the vertices whose associated orientation has both an in-branching and an out-branching. **Polynomial-time recognition conjecture.** There exists a polynomial algorithm for deciding whether a $2T$-graph has a good ordering. The paper presents this as an open problem about algorithmic recognition of good orientations in $2T$-graphs; no resolution is supplied in the source.
record.source_name: J. Bang-Jensen, S. Bessy, J. Huang and M. Kriesell, “Good orientations of 2T-graphs”, arXiv:1903.10287 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1903.10287

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2019).

record.title: The Seagull problem for graphs with independence number two
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph of order $n$, and let $\alpha(G)$ be its independence number and $\eta(G)$ its largest complete minor.

**Seagull problem.** For every graph $G$ with $\alpha(G)=2$, we have

$$
\eta(G) \ge \frac{n}{2}.
$$

This is equivalent to Hadwiger's conjecture in the case $\alpha(G)=2$. It is known when $G$ has no induced $C_4$ or induced $C_5$, but remains open in general.
record.source_name: Stijn Cambie, “Hadwiger's conjecture implies a conjecture of Füredi-Gyárfás-Simonyi”, arXiv:2108.10303 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.10303

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of August 2021). “On the other hand people who think Seagull's problem, Conjecture , is false and hence also Hadwiger's conjecture, may try to prove this by disproving the Conjecture from .”

record.title: Polynomial-time complexity of distance-$d$ independent set reconfiguration on trees under token sliding
record.statement: Let $d\geq 3$. In distance-$d$ independent set reconfiguration, denoted by $\textsc{D}d\textsc{ISR}$, configurations are distance-$d$ independent sets, and under the token-sliding rule, denoted by $\sfTS$, one token may slide along an edge in each move. The input graph is a tree. **Polynomial-time reconfiguration conjecture.** $\textsc{D}d\textsc{ISR}$ under $\sfTS$ on trees is in $\ttP$ for $d\geq 3$. The complexity of this problem is stated in the source to remain unknown, so this is an open problem concerning reconfiguration on trees.
record.source_name: Duc A. Hoang, “On the Complexity of Distance-d Independent Set Reconfiguration”, arXiv:2208.07199 (2024).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2021–2022). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2105.03402](https://arxiv.org/abs/2105.03402).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.07199

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2022).

record.title: Lovász–Mason contraction reduction for matroid symmetric powers
record.statement:
Let $M$ be a matroid on the ground set $E$, let $(M_1,\dots,M_d)$ be a symmetric quasi power of $M$, and suppose that $F\cdot\operatorname{Sym}_{d-1}(E)$ is a flat of $M_d$ for every flat $F$ of $M$. **Lovász–Mason contraction reduction.** There is an element $e\in E$ such that the contraction

$$
M_d\mathbin{\contr}\bigl(e\cdot\operatorname{Sym}_{d-1}(E)\bigr)
$$

is a symmetric quasi power of $M\mathbin{\contr}e$. This is presented as an auxiliary result sufficient to prove the Lovász–Mason flat-condition conjecture. Its resolution is not supplied in the given text, so it remains open here.
record.source_name: Nicholas Anderson, “Matroid Products in Tropical Geometry”, arXiv:2306.14771 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.14771

Status: **open** according to the source (as of June 2023). “Despite substantial effort, we were not able to make progress on this problem and have left it as an open problem left by Lov\'asz and Mason.”

record.title: Branch-depth as minor closure of contraction-deletion-depth
record.statement:
A matroid is a finite set equipped with a rank function satisfying the matroid axioms. Its **branch-depth** and **contraction-deletion-depth** are the graph- and matroid-depth parameters considered in the source. For a class of matroids, being **minor-closed** means that it contains every minor of each of its members.

**Branch-depth minor-closure conjecture.** There exists a function $f$ such that, if a matroid $M$ has branch-depth $d$, then there exists a matroid $N$ with contraction-deletion-depth at most $f(d)$ such that $M$ is a minor of $N$.

The result is proved in the paper for representable matroids, with an explicit bound on the contraction-deletion-depth of $N$. The conjecture asks whether the analogous statement holds for all matroids, possibly with a worse dependence on branch-depth.
record.source_name: Marcin Briański, Daniel Kráľ and Kristýna Pekárková, “Branch-depth is minor closure of contraction-deletion-depth”, arXiv:2402.16215 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.16215

Status: **open** according to the source (as of February 2024). “So, we pose the following as an open problem.”

record.title: $q$-analogue of the Erdős Matching Conjecture
record.statement:
Let $\mathbb{F}_q^n$ be the $n$-dimensional vector space over the finite field with $q$ elements, and let $\nu_q(\mathcal{V})$ denote the largest size of a matching of pairwise disjoint members of a family $\mathcal{V}$ of subspaces. **$q$-analogue Erdős Matching Conjecture.** If $\mathcal{V}$ is a family of $k$-dimensional subspaces of $\mathbb{F}_q^n$, $n\geq(s+1)k$, and $\nu_q(\mathcal{V})\leq s$, then

$$
|\mathcal{V}|\leq\min\left\{\genfrac{[}{]}{0pt}{}{n}{k}-\genfrac{[}{]}{0pt}{}{n-1}{k},\;s\genfrac{[}{]}{0pt}{}{n-1}{k-1}\right\}.
$$

The paper explicitly presents this as an open problem and as a $q$-analogue of the Erdős Matching Conjecture.
record.source_name: Jiuqiang Liu, Guihai Yu, Lihua Feng and Yongtao Li, “L-intersecting or Configuration Forbidden Families on Set Systems and Vector Spaces over Finite Fields”, arXiv:2403.04289 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.04289

Status: **open** according to the source (as of March 2024).

record.title: The constant-playability relaxation of the playable 1-2-3 conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a graph without isolated edges. For a function $f:E\rightarrow\mathbb{N}\cup\{0\}$, let $G$ be **$f$-unbalanceable** when $(G,\emptyset)$ is $(f,A)$-unbalanceable for arbitrarily chosen infinite sets $A\subseteq\mathbb{F}$.

**Constant-playability relaxation.** Let $G=(V,E)$ be a graph without isolated edges. Then there exists a constant $c\in\mathbb{N}\cup\{0\}$ such that $G$ is $f$-unbalanceable, where

$$
f:E\rightarrow\mathbb{N}\cup\{0\},\qquad f(e)=c\quad\text{for every }e\in E.
$$

The paper proposes this as a weaker relaxation because no constant bound is known for the online 1-2-3 conjecture problem. The source gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Marcin Anholcer, Bartłomiej Bosek, Grzegorz Gutowski, Michał Lasoń, Jakub Przybyło, Oriol Serra, Michał Tuczyński, Lluís Vena and Mariusz Zając, “Alon-Tarsi for hypergraphs”, arXiv:2501.00157 (2024).

record.title: Congested shallow-minor obstruction for toroidal graphs
record.statement:
A graph $H$ is a **congestion-$c$ depth-$d$ minor** of a graph $G$ if it has a congestion-$c$ depth-$d$ minor model in $G$: each vertex of $H$ is represented by a connected subgraph of $G$ of radius at most $d$, adjacent vertices of $H$ have intersecting or adjacent branch sets, and every vertex of $G$ belongs to at most $c$ branch sets.

**Toroidal shallow-minor conjecture.** There is no constant $k\in\mathbb N$ with the following property: every toroidal graph is a congestion-$k$ depth-$k$ minor of a planar graph.

This is proposed as a combinatorial stepping stone toward the surface transduction-order conjecture. The survey presents it as an open question.
record.source_name: Michał Pilipczuk, “Graph classes through the lens of logic”, arXiv:2501.04166 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.04166

Status: **open** according to the source (as of January 2025). “At the point of writing this survey, remains open and presents itself as the main algorithmic goal of the theory under development.”

record.title: Polynomial-time acyclic k-dicolouring conjecture for tournaments
record.statement:
For a tournament $T$, let $\vec{\chi}_{\rm a}(T)$ denote its acyclic dichromatic number. A fixed integer $k\geq3$ is treated as a constant rather than part of the input.

**Tournament acyclic dicolouring algorithm conjecture.** For every fixed $k\geq3$, it is polynomial-time decidable whether a tournament $T$ satisfies

$$
\vec{\chi}_{\rm a}(T)\leq k.
$$

The case $k=2$ is proved polynomial-time solvable in the paper, whereas the corresponding statement for every fixed $k\geq3$ is posed as an open complexity problem.
record.source_name: Jørgen Bang-Jensen, Lucas Picasarri-Arrieta and Anders Yeo, “Acyclic dichromatic number of oriented graphs”, arXiv:2511.20246 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.20246

Status: **open** according to the source (as of November 2025). “The conjecture remains open for every $k\geq 2$.”

record.title: Erdős Problem #128 — Dense Large Induced Subgraphs Force a Triangle
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite simple graph with $n$ vertices. Suppose that every vertex subset $V'$ satisfying
$$
2|V'|+1\ge n
$$
has an induced subgraph $G[V']$ with more than $n^2/50$ edges. Must $G$ contain a triangle?

record.title: Erdős Problem #742 — The Murty–Simon Diameter-Two-Critical Graph Conjecture
record.statement:
Let $V$ be a finite vertex type with decidable equality, let $G$ be a simple graph on $V$ with decidable adjacency relation, and suppose that $G$ has diameter $2$ and that, for every edge $e\in E(G)$, deleting $e$ produces a graph whose diameter is not $2$. Is it true that
$$|E(G)|\leq \left\lfloor\frac{|V|^2}{4}\right\rfloor?$$
